chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Those who sit under the Arak trees, those who settle beneath the Arak, have no Hajj.' He means whoever stands beneath it. But as for whoever settles beneath it and stands at the Station (of Arafat), there is no harm with him.
And the evidence for this is the first report.
And the Ghusl (ritual bath) on the Day of Arafah is after midday, and it is appropriate for a person to combine the two prayers so that he may be free for supplication.

key_terms.أَصْحَابَ الْأَرَكَ: Those who sit under the Arak trees
key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: Midday (when the sun begins to decline)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting under the Arak trees in Arafah during Hajj and when should the Ghusl be performed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic distinction between merely resting under the Arak trees, which some reports deem invalidating, and the proper ritual standing (wuquf) at the Station, which remains valid. It further prescribes performing Ghusl after midday on the Day of Arafah and advises combining Dhuhr and Asr prayers to maximize time for supplication (du'a), reflecting the Shia emphasis on spiritual preparation and the centrality of du'a in the Hajj rituals.
